summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant status, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for hyperglycemia caused by accidental use of an old insulin pump site. She presented with elevated blood glucose and a history of malaise and urinary frequency. In the hospital, her insulin pump site was replaced, leading to rapid improvement in glucose control. Labs showed resolution of any metabolic imbalance, and urine testing ruled out infection. Her thyroid function was found to be over-replaced, so her levothyroxine dose was reduced at discharge. She was medically stable, back to baseline, and discharged home with instructions to continue proper pump site management and follow up with her primary care and endocrinology providers.
